rejected.title: Choosing a display
card: Categorical
data sorts things into groups, such as favourite sport or type of pet. A bar chart or a pie chart suits it.
Numerical
data is a count or a measurement, such as height or test score. A histogram or a dot plot suits it and shows how the values spread out.
Over time
A line graph suits data that changes over time, such as a town's rainfall each month. The line keeps the times in order and shows the trend. A histogram or dot plot would lose that order.
To choose a display, first ask what type of data you have and what you want to show. Example: the number of students who walk, cycle or take the bus to school is categorical, so use a bar chart.
rejected.remember: Match the display to the data: groups, numbers or change over time.

a.q: Tamsin records the colour of each car that passes her school. What type of data is this, and which display suits it?
a.why: Car colour sorts cars into groups, so it is categorical data and a bar chart suits it. A histogram is for numerical data, such as counts or measurements, so it does not suit colours even though the data is correctly called categorical in that option.
a.clue: Is a colour a group or a measurement?

b.q: A council in Hobart records the city's mean daily temperature each month for three years. It wants to show how temperature changes over that time. Which display is best?
b.why: The data is recorded over time and the aim is to show change, so a line graph keeps the months in order and shows the trend. Temperature is numerical, which makes a histogram or dot plot tempting, but both would lose the order of the months.
b.clue: Which display keeps the months in order?

problems.detail: The distractor 'A dot plot of speeds' names data (speeds) that Tamsin did not record, so a student can rule it out without knowing which display suits categorical data. This leaves the question easier than it should be.

The distractors 'A bar chart of colours' and 'A histogram of one month' carry qualifiers that plainly do not fit temperatures over three years. 'A line graph' is the only plain option left, so it can be picked without knowing the idea.
The clue 'The aim is to show change over time' repeats the card's line-graph rule word for word, which gives the answer away.
